prerequisites: Knowledge and skills acquired in the basic mathematics and physics courses.

learning_outcomes.text: The student will know and understand the basic mathematical tools (vector calculus, applied vectors, geometry of areas).
The student will know and understand the kinematics and statics of systems of rigid bodies.
The student will know and understand the elastic problem of the one-dimensional beam.
The student will know and understand the fundamentals of Newtonian dynamics, with an outline of Lagrangian dynamics.

The student will know and understand the link between structure, function and mechanical properties of materials (elasticity, plasticity, viscoelasticity), with particular attention to biological tissues.

The student will know and understand the main failure modes of materials and the mechanisms governing the interaction between mechanical loadings and material response, including an outline of cellular mechanotransduction.
The student will be able to describe and solve simple equilibrium problems of statically determinate or under-constrained systems, in particular in the biomechanical field.
The student will be able to tackle problems concerning the equilibrium, kinematics and dynamics of the human body, also by means of structural analysis tools such as the Principle of Virtual Work.
The student will be able to draw free-body diagrams and determine constraint reactions and internal forces.
The student will be able to analyse simple trusses.

The student will be able to autonomously select the solution method best suited to the problem at hand, to evaluate the adequacy of the adopted biomechanical model and to judge the reliability and physical consistency of the results obtained.
The student will be able to present the methodologies adopted and the results obtained in a clear and conscious manner, with appropriate technical language, also by means of graphical works.

The student will develop the aptitude to autonomously search for solutions to problems not previously addressed or of an innovative nature, a necessary prerequisite for the subsequent courses and for future professional development.

syllabus_topics: Mathematical preliminaries (0.5 ECTS): Vector calculus and applied vectors; geometry of areas
Kinematics (1.0 ECTS): Kinematics of the point; rigid-body motion and particular rigid motions; displacements; constraints; settlements; degrees of freedom and degrees of lability
Statics (1.0 ECTS): Equations of statics and equilibrium conditions; free-body diagrams and constraint reactions; graphic statics; static–kinematic duality; principle of virtual work for rigid bodies
One-dimensional elastic beams (1.0 ECTS): Kinematics; internal force characteristics; constitutive law and elastic problem of the beam; identity of virtual works; trusses
Dynamics (0.5 ECTS): Review of Newtonian dynamics and outline of Lagrangian dynamics; applications to the rigid body and to one-dimensional systems

Mechanics of materials (1.0 ECTS): Outline of stress and strain analysis; mechanical properties of materials (elasticity, plasticity, viscoelasticity); failure modes (brittle and ductile fracture, viscoelastic failure, fatigue and creep); outline of the phenomenon of cellular mechanotransduction

assessment_methods.method: Oral test: discussion and in-depth examination of course themes

assessment_rules: The final mark is expressed on a scale of thirty (out of 30) and takes into account knowledge, application ability, communication and critical skills. The minimum learning level for a pass is 18/30, achieved when the student demonstrates adequate knowledge and understanding to describe and solve simple equilibrium problems of statically determinate or under-constrained systems, particularly in the biomechanical field. The maximum mark, possibly with honours (cum laude), is awarded for full command of course contents, methodological rigour, and command of language. Students with certified SLD, disabilities, or special educational needs should contact the professor and department coordinator early in the course to arrange suitable exam accommodations.
